_comment: Maintained by Claude — see ../CLAUDE.md 'Dashboard Maintenance' rule. Status values: concept | in-progress | review | ready | archived. Keys in 'mocks' are folder paths relative to products/Scheduling/ (no trailing /index.html).

recentChanges.summary: Preview Mode button now opens a full simulation modal (not just a visual toggle). The modal shows: a hypothetical scenario card (overtime fire watch, 12-hour sick relief, mutual-aid standby — cyclable), the predicted call order computed from the in-progress rule, a two-step dispatch flow (decline → next person accepts) that reflects the rule's decline-action setting, and an 'Ask the AI a specific scenario' panel with sample question chips ('What if the top 3 decline?', tie handling, fiscal reset, PTO) plus a freeform input. AI answers are generated by a local pattern matcher that consults the user's actual rule fields, so the preview feels rule-aware.

Added a Preview Mode toggle button to the top-right of the rule-builder dual-screen header banner. Hovering it reveals a dark tooltip describing the tool ('Optional exercise for all rule activations and edits. Simulates ranking outcomes before go-live. For customers with no historical data, the system provides generic, appropriate hypothetical scenarios. The customer can also ask the AI chat how the rule would handle specific scenarios that they provide.'). Clicking flips the button to an inverted white/purple 'ON' state so users can see they're in preview mode.

Rule Type dropdown in the right-panel config now mirrors the six prompt names (Standard Rolodex, Accumulating Rolodex, Accumulation — Hours Based, Static — Seniority Based, Static — By Employee ID, Random / Lottery, Custom) so the selected option matches the card the user clicked. Restructured the panel so the Rule Summary / Preview Ranking lives inside the scroll area with position:sticky — it scrolls up with content and a scroll listener auto-collapses it into a compact pill once you scroll past 36px (re-expands near the top), freeing vertical room on a laptop. Added per-prompt call-and-response fields (post-accept move + response window, accumulation type + limit, reset cadence + outcomes counted, seniority date type, sort direction + new-hire placement + case handling, randomize frequency + weighting + guardrail) so answering chat chips reveals new fields on the right.

Ported the full Rules Engine prototype (CallBack dashboard, Rule Builder, Approaches & Rules, History) into the test mock — rewrote the React app as vanilla HTML/JS using Vector web components for form inputs while preserving the original purple AI gradient palette, friendly chip styles, and animated reveal feel.

Approaches & Rules 'Add New Rule' banner now shows only the three first-page chips (Standard Rolodex, Accumulating Rolodex, Accumulation — Hours Based) with no 'Something else' toggle, and the freeform input is highlighted (pencil icon, tinted gradient background, glow ring) so it reads as an invitation to write your own rule.

Reworked the 6 'Help me build a rule based on' prompts to mirror today's rule types — Standard Rolodex, Accumulating Rolodex, Accumulation — Hours Based (page 1) and Static — Seniority Based, Static — By Employee ID, Random / Lottery (page 2) — across the dashboard, in-builder suggestions, and Approaches & Rules chip banner. Each prompt now triggers its own tailored follow-up flow. Restructured the right-side panel: Preview Ranking and Rule Summary live in tabs (preview first) so the live ranking is visible while the AI builds; new compact header reads 'Rule configuration: editable updates live as you chat' with a minimal collapse chevron; tightened paddings so the panel doesn't feel cramped on a laptop when the summary is open.

Each of the 6 AI prompts now triggers its own distinct follow-up flow (Rolodex, Hours, Turns, Seniority, Reliability, Workload Spread) — no more shared default questions. Rolodex flow now asks the post-callback movement question (back / stay / custom). Swapped 'Detail Coverage' → 'Reliability Based' and 'Forced Rest' → 'Workload Spread'.
Swapped Skill Based + Static List prompts for 'Detail / Event Coverage' and 'Forced Rest Window' — both more grounded in real fire/EMS callback operations.

Reworked AI chat prompts per Shannon's interview (Rolodex decline-behavior, hours-based reset + seniority fallback, turn-based shift-length caveat, per-rank seniority); softened intro from 'template' to 'Try one of these prompts'; right-side Rule Config panel now auto-scrolls when new fields reveal.
Linked the Rules Engine mock to Jira ticket UX-2258.
Moved Theme Colors to concept status.
Moved AI Search Engine Dashboard to concept status.
Created a new test / scratch space from the base template.
Stood up the auto-syncing prototype index dashboard.
